s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory distress with a subcutaneous mass in the cervical region
salient_findings: Subcutaneous mass in the ventral cervical region
Mild leukocytosis with neutrophilia and lymphopenia
key_facts: 1-week history of dyspnea and inspiratory noise
Esophageal obstruction was suspected but not confirmed
Subcutaneous mass is 10 × 8 × 3-cm, partially firm and fluctuant, and mildly warm
Normal vital signs and good body condition
No dysphagia, other masses, or lymphadenopathy detected
Mild leukocytosis with neutrophilia and lymphopenia
Eosinophils are decreased
Hematocrit is 39.8%
MCV is mildly increased, and MCHC is mildly decreased
Flexible endoscopy of the esophagus and trachea showed no abnormalities
Cervical ultrasonography showed a well-demarcated, heterogeneously echogenic, encapsulated mass
